newsitem.title: UK: Eurostar dismisses UK attack over illegal migrants.
newsitem.headline: Eurostar dismisses UK attack over illegal migrants.

text.p: Cross-channel train operator Eurostar on Thursday dismissed a fierce attack by a British minister who accused the company of not doing enough to deter illegal migrants travelling from Paris to London.

Home Office (interior) Minister Mike O'Brien, responding to a rise in the number of Eurostar passengers arriving without documents in London and then claiming asylum, said the company had refused to introduce passport and visa checks in Paris.
But a Eurostar official said it was up to British immigration authorities to check travellers' documents.
"We are not by law obliged to carry out these checks," he said by telephone.
"Should documentation not be in order, or on arrival should a passenger seek political asylum, it is for the authorities to decide whether they are granted entry."
Eurostar insiders say document checks in Paris would result in long queues and make the service less attractive to passengers. Around 500,000 people use the London to Paris service each month.
"We are a bit bewildered by this. We have always worked with the Home Office on this and we want to sort the matter out," the official said.

O'Brien lashed out at Eurostar on Wednesday after talks with immigration officers at London's Waterloo station, who reported a sharp rise in the number of Somali immigrants arriving without any papers.
"The Immigration Service is frustrated by the lack of cooperation from Eurostar," he said afterwards.
"This is of great concern to us. Over a period of time we have been asking Eurostar to take steps to improve controls. They have not done so. They comply only with their legal obligations."
Eurostar is currently exempt from fines imposed on airlines that fail to check the documents of passengers, but O'Brien said this could be reviewed.
Between January and June this year 510 people including 229 Somalis claimed asylum on arrival at Waterloo. So far this month, 131 Somalis and 86 dependants have asked for asylum at the station.
"The vast majority of the Somalis are arriving without any documents at all," said a Home Office spokesman.
"There are clear indications that there is an organised racket transporting people here without passports," he said by telephone.

One Somali woman seeking asylum told the Daily Telegraph newspaper that her journey had been arranged by middlemen in Addis Ababa who had charged her 925 pounds ($1,510) for a faked passport and a ticket to France.

O'Brien said the government also wanted immigration service staff to train Eurostar check-in personnel, and said notices outlining British document requirements should be displayed at international stations.
Eurostar is owned by the London and Continental railways consortium, which includes National Express Group Plc and Virgin Group. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
